Nodes.Text:
"Then listen. That forest could not feed half the army the writer marched through it."
{n}She opens the book and finds the offending passage. The evening goes pleasantly enough for her to miss the first bell. She goes back to her lodging before the second.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Irabeth
Nodes.Text:
{n}She lifts the pack again.{/n}
"Then you should have read my letter. Goodnight, Commander."

Paragraphs.Text: {n}Irabeth never resumed her commission in Drezen. The corrected account stayed with the quartermaster. Her letters came from the road, with no rank beneath the signature.{/n}

{n}After the war she came through Drezen again, dusty and cross about a flooded road. The Commander met her at the gate. She kissed a familiar mouth before beginning her complaint, then insisted on hearing what had happened to the carter.{/n}
{n}She left again for the home she kept with Anevia. There were more visits, and letters when a visit could not happen. The betrayal at the Coronation stayed between them; she never called an evening its pardon.{/n}

{n}They stayed correspondents. Irabeth sent the passages she objected to, along with invitations to argue about them. The Commander answered. Her wife kept her place at the other end of every journey.{/n}
{n}When the Commander died, Irabeth wrote no invitation. She kept the last answer inside the book, and went home to mourn without a military audience.{/n}
{n}After the ascension she addressed her letters to the same name, not the new temple. She still served Iomedae. She expected her own letters to be answered, however far the road had become.{/n}
{n}When Anevia died, Irabeth kept her wedding ring. The next invitation was for company; she made no promise on behalf of the woman she had lost.{/n}
